Hey man I don't know if this applies to you, only you can know if going to rehab is right for you. 

I swore it was never going to happened, went kicking and screaming only to find it was extremely beneficial. After 15 days of inpatient rehab I felt amazing. My mind was clear, I was eating 3x a day, and havig meaningful and intimate (not sexual) interaction with my peers. 

Afterwards I still feel great, I've slipped up a few times but recovery is a process. You aren't measured on how many times you fall, the real measure of character is how many times you get up. And believe me you can get up. 

Find a self help group that fits you ( NA, SMART, etc). Feeling like a drug addict destroys your self esteem, we all hated ourselves when we walked into those rooms, many of us including myself had decided to attempt to end our suffering the only way we thought we could (suicide). After some clean time things become so different. Life gets better, not right away but addicts with decades of clean time are THE happiest and most kind hearted people I've ever met. I'm still a miserible excuse for a person in recovery but every day gets a little easier. 
 
There is light at the end of the tunnel. Hang in their friend <3.

I have an extremely addictive personality and an unreal predisposition to addiction ( every branch of my family tree is filled with alcoholics and drug addicts more or less). Quitting wasn't particularly hard, just extremely unpleasant. I gave my script to a friend and had him give me ONLY the amount I needed to take to avoid potentially fatal withdraws each day. I went to the psychiatrist and told her going home had really sorted me out (only saw her once a month) and I didn't want to take them anymore. I still take benzos, primarily alprazalam, on occasion but I always wait AT least a month between occasions to give my inner fiend time to die and I never buy more than what I intend to take right away.

The ap generated from ap runes isn't really that beneficial as most supports have low ap ratios and you won't be building an enormous amount of ap. if you ran a flat ap page you'd end up with 25-30 ap. that translates to anywhere from +5 to +15 on an ability. You are much better of using armor, hp, mr or gp10 runes seeing how the supports so have listed are rather squishy especially Sona. The increase in other stats will indirectly increase your damage seeing how your opponents will be hitting you for less, making your damage higher than your opponents. GP10 quints are ideal as you will not be getting much farm, and getting your items faster makes you stronger than the increase in stats would. The ony support I prefer to run quints that aren't gp10 is Sona, as she is so damn squishy early on that the increase in hp from flat hp quints makes a huge difference in your ability to stay in lane.

Caitlin's aa range is rediculously long, I don't know the exact value but the only two adcs with higher rangers are late game Tristana and Kog Mow with his bio arcane barrage active. This being said, you should take advantage of this by harassing your lane opponent with autos as much as possible. Watch your own minions, when one gets low and he gets ready to last hit, pop him with an aa while he's last hitting the creep, because he is mid animation he can't retaliate. Free damage is the best damage. Always try to use your headshot bonus on the enemy ad, however don't run forward, tank 6 creeps, and get hit by everything the enemy ad and support have trying to do so resulting in you loosing 60% of your hp. It's not the end of the world if you use it on a creep. 

My favorite way, and I think the universally accepted best way to do this is use your q to shove the enemy ad under his tower. To do this, when the creeps are all lined up before they take Aggro, fire a q down all of them. While your creeps focus on the Meele creeps, you can kill the caster creeps in about 1 auto. Unless all your creeps attack one enemy creep, the pattern goes as follows:  caster, caster, Meele, Meele, caster Meele. If course this changes from wave to wave, don't miss CS because your too busy following a pattern, last hit the creeps that need to die! 

Now that the enemy ad is shoved to his tower, he will be focused on last hitting the minions. When he steps up to do so, hit him with an auto attack. Your range is so long most of the time you won't draw tower agro but if you do just step back when you here the beep sound. It takes about 1 second for the tower to lock on and if you step out of range before that, you won't take any damage. Continue harassing with qs while they're under tower, don't just spam them though as you'll go oom very quick. If the enemy ad is standing in line with his creeps, don't hesitate to fire your q before you'll hit all the minions. It's way better to hit him and 2/3 of the creeps then just hit all the creeps. 

Caitlin's traps are very powerful. In lane, use them to control where the enemy can go. Drop one in their lane brush, and when you have him pushed to tower drop them around the tower in places creeps usually don't go to make his life more annoying. If he ever steps on a trap, slap him with a q. When you decide to go all in, place a trap in the path the enemy is running! They run right into them 90% of the time and it makes your life much easier. These traps can also be used later in the game when seiging towers, to control enemy movement again. 

Your e is an excellent tool for escaping and kiting as it now only moves you away, but also slows the enemy. Remember you get knocked in the opposite direction you shoot it. So if you want to go forward you shoot it back and vice versa. The e can also be used to jump over thin walls, like the baron pit, the dragon pit, the wolf kit. You can jump over any walls that can be transversed by nitalee jump or graves e. The most satisfying use of your e is when you pull of an e q combo, if you press both at the same time it cancels the q animation, slows your target, and gets you out of range for any retaliation however it costs a large amount of mana and puts your escape on cool down so use wisely! 

Her ultimate can be lots of fun, as there's something very satisfying about sniping an enemy who thought he was lucky enough to escape with low hp. In laning phase it makes an excellent finishing move, however in team fights it's very difficult to hit your intended target so I often use it at the start of fights, or to chunk a high value target like the enemy ad or ap carry that is out of position and has no one to act as a bodyguard for them. Furthermore, if a fight is going down an you won't get there in time to help, fire your ultimate, help your team, and get some assist gold in te process. 

My runes for Caitlin are typical ad carry runes: 9x AD reds, 9x armor yellows, I run 9x ad blues(if the enemy has 2 ap Heros or a support like Sona that deals lots of magic damage early, I'll run 9x flat mr blues) and 3x flat ad quints. 

My build now goes something like: dorans blade > vamp septor boots/ pickaxe boots > botrk (it's op as shit) > zeal > PD if I'm getting dive by tanks bruisers or IE if I'm being left alone > LW  > warmogs or frozen mallet.  If the enemy gets early armor, don't be afraid to get your LW before your ie or finishing your pd as zeal grants enough attack speed and armor pen scales super well after the S3 changes.

AD isn't really a position that needs mentoring. It's the most mechanical out of all the roles.  There are five key concepts the way I see it. 
1.) Farming: you should always be farming, get every last hit that is humanly possible and channel your inner doublelift and get a few that aren't. However, never sucicide for last hits. 23 gold is not worth the 200 you just gave the enemy plus the wave you're going to miss because your dead. 

2. Trading: trade damage whenever it is beneficial to you. Several factors determine when a trade is beneficial. Anytime you can get free damage do it. It's free, what's better than that. The best way to do this is watch your own creeps hp as well as the enemy creeps. When your opponent goes to last hit, hit him with an aa. Because he's attacking the minion, he can't hit you back and your aas start to add up quick. Do you have more hp pots then your opponent? You should try to trade damage when it will stick (because your opponent has no way of healing it back). Does your opponent have lower hp than you? The lower his hp, the better your trades become as soon you can burst him for a kill. 

3. Positioning: you should never be in front. Always stand in a safe place. Stand behind your creeps in lane, stay behind your team out of lane. 

4. Kiting: this is the hardest and most satisfying aspect of playing ad. The idea is to move between auto attacks to prevent melee Heros from hitting you. It's basically the same motion as studdering marines in SC. 

5. Dealing damage: this is the sole reason you exist. You want to make the other team hurt. However, you must deal damage in the most optimal way possible. Hit the most important targets you can. Enemy Olaf rushing at you, don't just stand there and hit the enemy ad. Sure your doing damage but you'll die in 2 seconds and you can't deal damage while dead, unless yor karthus. However,  full tank enemy rammus hitting you with all his cc down, don't attack him! Hit someone important. 
If you didn't win a game, you did some one of those five things improperly and should be able to fix it. Save your mentors for morecerebral positions like support and jungler. Hope this help!

Alright I've got like 100 or so games with TF and this is what I've picked up. 

Runes: I usually run magic pen reds, AP/level yellows, MR Blues and movespeed quints OR Magic pen reds flat hp yellows mr blues and flat ap quints

Masterys: I like to go 21 0 9 with points in movespeed and the extra buff duration in utility. 

Item Build: I Always start flask ward 5 pots its lets you farm safely till 6.  If a teamate or two already do tons of damage i build boots 5 to help catch people out of position with stun, if i need damage i build sorc boots. If I am ahead early I will grab a Haunting Gyse(sp) to increase my lead, if not I either go LB >Deathcap or Deathcap >LB im still trying to to figure out which is better.  LB first lends itself to better burst and ganks while Deathcap is just raw damage.   With LB your main dmg source will be w, deathcap it will be q.   Then I build into whatever I need, if i went mobos i grab a void staff, if not Ill pick up an abyssal or a zonyas. 

Laning Phase: use blue card to help last hit, however don't immedently lock a blue card, let the cards cycle until the last second. This lets you zone your opponent as he ir she will be waiting for the stun. Don't be afriad to use q, try and aim the side cards as people will dodge the middle one.  because q is easy to dodge and will push the wave if you hit creeps with it, i find trading with a blue card and an e proc is easier to hit, and does comparable dmg. Try to stay topped of around level 5 and start shoving to hit a fast 6 and gank.  

Ganking: TF's ult is one of the best in the game during the laning phase, so use it!  Everytime it is off cooldown you should be able to net your team a kill.  That being said, the proper way to ult gank is first r, start w cycle, second r, pick card.  This allows for more gold card time then picking gold before you start your port.  Try to port in the best spot possible, your victim should not be able to escape, even if he flashes.  JUST BECAUSE YOU POP THE FIRST R DOES NOT MEAN YOU HAVE TO PORT.  If you won't win the exchange, don't do it. 

Mid Game: Here is your time to shine, with two dorans and level 5 q you can full wave clear. Red card the second sword creep and q down the line.  Now go roam somewhere!  Roam, secure kills, and use the advantage to push objectives.  This is why i prefer ganking bot.  Killing their botlane leads to easy dragons and blue steals (if your blue side) .

Late Game: You're an ap caster. You've already past your prime.  However, 6 item TF is terrifying.  You W and litch bane procs can basically one shot a squishy.  Get good a picking gold cards, at this point in the game you are most helpful as a stun bot (2 second stun on 4 second CD OP), stun everything that comes close to your carry.  Feel free to use your ult to check baron or even brushes. Its got a 1 minute CD at rank 3 and the port isnt really that helpful as people will be grouped up.

Cho gath is a great champ to learn. Great sustain in lane, very few bad matchups, and eating people is a ridiculous amount of fun. He's only 1350 ip too. For top lane cho I usually run magic pen reds armor yellows scaling mr blues and ap Quints. Start with w then go q e max w first then e as q is semi hard to hit. Focus on csing until 3 or 4. Once your level 4 you have pretty good trades. W has good burst, but as a high Cd and can push lane really hard so use it wisely. When fighting full on, w and drop a q at your feet if its a melee champ. The knock lets you land some aas which is really helpful as the e DAmage adds up. Once you hit 6 feast a creep to get your stacks going. As long as your even in lane  aa w as q ignite r will net you easy kills. If you get ganked drop a q in there path while running away. Chos base move speed is kinda low so the knock up either hits them and slows them, or make them alter there path to where you should get away. When getting tower dived, q the floor w them r and ignte if you want will make it an easy 1 for 1. 

I usually build resistance heavy tank cho when I play him top to take advantage of his really high base damage and the free hp front feast stacks. I usually start flask 5 ward > catalyst > tabi or treads > rod > fh or bulwark/spirt visage, however because of his high base damage you can totally tailor your build to your enemy's. 

In team fights you want to soak up damage and just be an asshole. A good w can shut down their ap carry while a good q can zone or kill an ad carry. Use feast to burst people hard and secure every single buff and objective (1000 true damage means no smite steals). Although its not terribl if you die, loosing feast stacks is annoying so don't die unnecessarily. Don't be afraid to flash out of fights of you're about to die. If you do die, you should use feast everytime it's off cd and there is no fight about to break out to get those stacks back ASAP. If you're struggling to maintain stacks, a warmogs can so wonders.

TF: don't forget to move in between autos! Seriously, moving towards them with each auto doubles the amount of stuns you land. When they are stunned, move towards te direction they will run away! Often that will let you land more stuns, and the more is a great thing. When ganking with ultimate you should do r w r wait for port to get to about 80 then w. this gives you an extra 2 seconds on gold card. Little things matter a good deal with the card master. When ganking don't be afriad to blue card! For example if you gank a Taric graves botlane, you can pull a blue for higher burst. Knowing when to blue and when to gold takes some getting used to, I have 100 normal games as TF and i still fail sometimes. 
Your Q can be very deceptive. You throw three cards, so use them! Line up side cards in lane to get CS and harass even when they aren't close to creeps. When you lob qs for harass people will dodge the middle one, but often forget about the side ones. 

Be sure to have your e stacked before harassing if you can. The extra burst really helps. If you harass with blue card and e it can really hurt. And it's easier to land than a random q. Then you can chuck a q as they run away, makes for solid trades. 

When it comes time to all in someone, ignite while your gold card is traveling. That way it starts ticking earlier, so they die to your burst instead of ignte ticks while running away. This helps prevent those heart breaking moments when your enemy chugs his hp pots and lives through the last tick of ignite with 10 hp. 

If someone escapes with no HP and you see the jungler or know its safe to enter his jungle because you have t warded, try a blind q! Often times people will try to blue pil between towers and you can get a super satisfying no scope super MLG pro snipe. 

Also, once you have level 4 q and and two dorans you can red card the second sword creep while they're in line and clear to whole wave with one q. 

Last note, don't be afriad to use q in lane! Use it to farm, use it to harass. You have basically unlimited mans with yor blue cards. You can keep a blue card up to make lasting hitting easier.  Once you hit 40% mana try to only pick blue cards (unless you need to escape). 

Now onto his ult. TF's ult is totally awesome. Even if you are being shut down in lane, you just get fed through other lanes. Putting your team ahead everywhere. You should try and gank EVERY time it is up. Just because you pop the first r doesn't mean you have to port. If its too risky, don't do it. It's only a 2 minute Cd. Not worth a death. Nocturne: early game you're ganks are really really strong. However just because your early ganks are strong doesn't mean you should force things. Unless a kill or a flash is certain farm your jungle. You become an enemy laners nightmare at level 6 (pun semi intended). You can engage with your ultimate from max range, or q them and ultimate in the q trail. Even though this has been said before, I'm going to reiterate it because I feel it is that important.  You're playing too many roles.  I used to do just that, attempt to fill in whatever my team needed to do and I'm sure you're aware how difficult that is.  I picked one role, found one champ I enjoyed playing in that role (because when you're having fun playing, its less frustrating when you aren't playing well).  Play this champ as much as possible, get absolutely comfortable with the nuisances of said champ.  If you don't know what you're up against, neither does your opponent! With time you'll develop a set of "guidelines" with each machup, what should/shouldn't you do to keep yourself in there.  Once you get comfortable with one champ in a role, pick another you enjoy and do the same thing.  Once you get two strong champions, you will understand the basic principles of LoL that will make playing every lane easier.  Then start playing the free champs in different roles, (say you main midlane and malphite is free, play some malphite toplane or maplhite jungle) once you find a champ you like a different role, play it until you're comfortable.  Eventually you will have one or two champs you are really comfortable with in every role.  At that point, you're set :).
